items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: Mason is all right, there's a lot of crap too.

ctx.x: would be money. I mean it. Well, nothing against it. In this day and age I'm not leaving my wife

at home at night to go play around in blue lodges. I'm a Shrine and all that. Mason is all right, there's a lot of crap too. But I'd rather stay home so my wife is safe. She's by herself and we live in the damn big house and leave a thousand burglaries. So I'm not coming with you. I don't need any money. But if I'm going to put up with that stuff, I go to the convention. I pay my way and then I play music. For what? Nobody else plays. Are they down to dancing? And we damn fools wept. They're playing. And half the…

I don't like to talk. I don't have a stick. Sure. I'm curious to know about some of the other orchestras. How would you describe Robichaux and the kind of jobs, what kind of jobs did he get, do you know of, and Perrone? Well, as I told you, I was- You're so busy yourself.
